h: Oral albuterol overuse: expected finding?
p: Beta-2 agonists cause tachycardia, tremor and hypokalemia (K+ shifts into cells), never hyperkalemia.

h: Von Willebrand disease: which factor is secondarily low?
p: vWF carries and stabilizes factor VIII, so deficiency prolongs bleeding time and PTT. Desmopressin releases stored vWF; avoid aspirin.

h: Hands in ice water, core temperature steady: mechanism?
p: Sympathetic cutaneous vasoconstriction reduces heat loss from skin; shivering is a later response to falling core temperature.

h: Major depression sleep study: expected finding?
p: Depression shortens REM latency, increases REM density and total REM, reduces slow-wave sleep and causes early morning awakening.

h: Weak PIP flexion with intact DIP flexion: injured muscle?
p: FDS flexes the proximal interphalangeal joints; FDP flexes the distal interphalangeal joints.

h: Mitral regurgitation: best auscultation site?
p: Mitral regurgitation gives a holosystolic apical murmur radiating to the axilla with a soft S1 and S3; endocarditis is a classic cause.

h: After splenectomy for trauma: which vaccine is needed?
p: Asplenia risks encapsulated organisms (pneumococcus, Hib, meningococcus), so give pneumococcal, Hib and meningococcal vaccines, ideally 2 weeks after (or before elective) splenectomy.

h: Graft clots minutes after clamp release: rejection mechanism?
p: Hyperacute rejection from preformed anti-donor antibodies (ABO or HLA) causes thrombosis within minutes to hours; the graft must be removed.

h: Isotretinoin in a woman of childbearing age: pair with which drug?
p: Isotretinoin is highly teratogenic (iPLEDGE requires two contraceptive methods and pregnancy tests); also causes dry skin, hypertriglyceridemia and mood effects.

h: Spinal cord hemisection: which side loses pain and temperature below the lesion?
p: Brown-Sequard: ipsilateral weakness and loss of vibration and proprioception below the lesion; contralateral pain and temperature loss starting 1-2 levels below.

h: Ebstein anomaly: which maternal drug exposure?
p: First-trimester lithium is linked to Ebstein anomaly (atrialized right ventricle, tricuspid regurgitation). Valproate causes neural tube defects; warfarin causes nasal hypoplasia and bone defects.

h: Indinavir: signature adverse effect?
p: Indinavir crystallizes in urine, causing kidney stones (hydrate well); protease inhibitors also cause hyperglycemia and lipodystrophy. Pancreatitis is classic for didanosine.

h: Skin-crawling sensation, dilated pupils, diaphoresis at a party: substance?
p: Cocaine intoxication: sympathetic excess with formication ('cocaine bugs'), mydriasis, hyperthermia and hypertension.

h: First-line oral type 2 diabetes drug: mechanism?
p: Metformin activates AMPK, lowers hepatic glucose output and improves insulin sensitivity; risk of lactic acidosis, weight neutral.

h: Rifampin: target and process disrupted?
p: Rifampin inhibits DNA-dependent RNA polymerase. It induces CYP450 and turns body fluids orange.

h: Pregnant woman seizing with BP 186/97 and RUQ pain: first drug?
p: Eclampsia is treated with magnesium sulfate for seizure control and prophylaxis, plus blood pressure control; delivery follows maternal stabilization.

h: Diphtheria toxin: molecular target?
p: The A subunit ADP-ribosylates eEF-2, halting protein synthesis (also Pseudomonas exotoxin A). Pseudomembrane, bull neck; alpha-amanitin hits RNA polymerase II.

h: Bubonic plague in a camper (Yersinia pestis): reservoir?
p: Y. pestis is spread by fleas from rodents; presents with painful buboes. Treat with streptomycin or gentamicin; doxycycline is an alternative.

h: Consciously postponing worry about grades to finish an essay: defense mechanism?
p: Suppression is conscious and mature; denial and repression are unconscious. Dissociation is a temporary drastic change in identity or awareness.

h: Holosystolic murmur louder on inspiration, JVD, hepatomegaly: predisposing factor?
p: Tricuspid regurgitation (Carvallo sign) after S. aureus tricuspid endocarditis in IV drug users; rheumatic fever mainly damages the mitral valve.

h: Shock-related tubular cell swelling: mechanism?
a: Failure of Na+/K+-ATPase from ATP depletion
p: Ischemia depletes ATP, the pump fails, sodium and water enter, and cells swell (reversible injury). Caspases drive apoptosis, not this swelling.

h: Tense bullae in an elderly patient, Nikolsky negative: antibody target?
p: Bullous pemphigoid: IgG against BP180/BP230 at the dermal-epidermal junction (subepidermal bullae). Pemphigus targets desmosomes (intraepidermal, Nikolsky positive).

h: Pre-B acute lymphoblastic leukemia: flow cytometry markers?
p: B-ALL is TdT+, CD10+, CD19+; T-ALL expresses CD3/CD7; CD56 marks NK cells. Pediatric ALL has a good prognosis, with t(12;21) favorable.

h: RA drug causing mouth ulcers and raised transaminases: mechanism?
p: Methotrexate toxicity: mucositis, hepatotoxicity, myelosuppression, pneumonitis; folic acid or leucovorin helps rescue.
